headys_lumen.config.title: Heady's Lumen: ShaderLights
headys_lumen.config.handheld.help: How the light in your hand reaches the shader pack. Each item's own intensity, colour and flicker are on the Light items tab.
headys_lumen.config.enabled.tooltip: Master switch. When off, the mod does nothing.
headys_lumen.config.match_suffix.tooltip: Modded items light up without being in your list, acting as their vanilla light: ids ending in soul_torch or soul_lantern (cyan), redstone_torch (red), sea_lantern, jack_o_lantern or lantern, and copper_torch or copper_lantern (green). Any other id ending in torch acts as a normal torch. Vanilla items are left alone unless you add them to your Light items list.
headys_lumen.config.light_level.tooltip: Light level (1-15) for auto-detected plain torches. The other auto-detected kinds use their vanilla level (soul 10, redstone 7, lanterns 15, copper torch 14).
headys_lumen.config.spoof_id: Pretend to be a normal torch
headys_lumen.config.spoof_id.tooltip: Held and placed: tells the shader pack the item is minecraft:torch when nothing better applies, so you get the pack's torch light. Skipped if the pack already knows the item.
headys_lumen.config.send_color.tooltip: Passes each item's colour to Iris' heldBlockLightColor value. Shader packs that read it show your exact colour. Needs "colored lighting" in the pack to be on.
headys_lumen.config.nearest_item: Match closest item (packs without colour support)
headys_lumen.config.nearest_item.tooltip: Held and placed: for packs that colour lights per item or block, the shader is told it is whichever vanilla light the pack knows with the closest colour. Use "Pretend to be" on an item to choose it yourself.
headys_lumen.config.items.tooltip: Press + to add an item. Press X on a row to remove it.
headys_lumen.config.items.help: Press + to add a row. Each row is one item: its ID, how bright it is, what colour, and optionally which item the shader should think it is.
headys_lumen.config.item.id.tooltip: e.g. examplemod:blue_torch. Vanilla items work too: add minecraft:torch with a colour to recolour torches. You can use * as a wildcard (examplemod:*_lamp). /lumen addheld adds the item in your hand. Blocks without an item (lava, fire, soul fire, nether portal) work by their block id, e.g. minecraft:lava: that changes the light they cast when placed, in packs with the light table (the PhotonFork).
headys_lumen.config.item.intensity.toolt: Held light level 1-15, used exactly: it can also dim an item that already glows by itself. 0 = no held light at all, for items such as unlit or burnt-out torches (e.g. *:unlit_torch). Heady's Lumen: ShaderPack_PhotonFork uses it for brightness AND reach. Photon, Solas and Rethinking Voxels ignore it; in Rethinking Voxels the mod dims the colour instead.
headys_lumen.config.item.use_color.toolt: Off = the shader pack picks the colour. On = use the Hue and Saturation sliders below.
headys_lumen.config.item.hue.tooltip: Slide to pick the colour. The label and the Preview box show what you are picking.
headys_lumen.config.item.saturation.tool: 0 = white light, 100 = fully coloured. The Preview box shows hue + saturation + intensity together.
headys_lumen.config.item.pretend.tooltip: For shader packs that colour held lights per item. Pick an item the pack knows (e.g. minecraft:sea_lantern for a cyan glow). Empty = automatic. Type any item id or choose from the list.
headys_lumen.config.item.flicker.tooltip: Follow group: the Flicker tab decides (its groups, Immersion mode or all lights), with its default speed and strength. On: always flickers, with the two sliders below. Off: never (unless the Flicker tab is set to all lights). Held light: shows in packs that use the held light level (PhotonFork, Complementary, BSL, KappaPT) and in Rethinking Voxels. Placed: only in the PhotonFork.
headys_lumen.config.item.flicker_speed.t: How fast it flickers: 1 = a slow waver, 20 = a fast, nervous flame. Only used when Flicker is on.
headys_lumen.config.item.flicker_strengt: How much it dims at its darkest, as a share of the Intensity: 35% of intensity 14 dips to about 9. Shader packs only take whole light levels, so a weak flicker on a low intensity may barely show. Only used when Flicker is on.
headys_lumen.config.invalid_id: Invalid item id. Use modid:item (lowercase letters, digits, _ . - / and * wildcards).
headys_lumen.config.missing_cloth.1: The in-game editor needs Cloth Config.
headys_lumen.config.missing_cloth.2: Install it, or edit config/lumen.json and use /lumen reload.
headys_lumen.config.rgb_id_mode.tooltip: Rethinking Voxels reads the item id as a colour, so the mod can send your EXACT colour (16 steps per channel) by choosing the id. Auto-detect checks the pack's ids for torch / soul torch / redstone torch. Use 'Always on' if detection misses your pack.
headys_lumen.config.match_rendered: Also change how the item is drawn
headys_lumen.config.match_rendered.toolt: Some packs (such as current Rethinking Voxels releases) only light the hand when the item being DRAWN looks like a light source. With this on, your items are drawn as the vanilla light they pose as (your "Pretend to be", else the closest colour, else a torch). Turn it off if a pack makes your items look wrong.
headys_lumen.config.placed.help: Placed modded torches and lanterns glow like the vanilla light they act as, using the same rules as your held lights: your Light items list ("Pretend to be", or the closest colour) and auto-detect. Colours come from the shader pack's own table, and the brightness is the block's own (with the PhotonFork: your exact colour and intensity). Saving reloads the world's chunks once (like F3+A).
headys_lumen.config.placed_lights.toolti: Shader packs only know vanilla light blocks. With this on, placed modded torches and lanterns get the id of the vanilla light they act as, so the pack gives them its coloured light. It also stops packs such as Kappa from treating a modded torch as a solid block that casts a full block of shadow.
headys_lumen.config.placed_recolor_vanil: If your Light items list gives a vanilla item a colour or a "Pretend to be" (e.g. a pink minecraft:torch), placed blocks of it change too. Off: only your held item changes.
headys_lumen.config.placed_flicker.toolt: Lights that flicker (see the Flicker tab and each item's Flicker setting) also flicker when placed. Only in shader packs built for it (Heady's Lumen: ShaderPack_PhotonFork); other packs show them steady. The shader pack animates it, so it costs no extra performance.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.help: Which lights flicker like a flame, in your hand and placed. Rows in Light items set to "Follow group" (the default) and lights that are not in your list follow this tab; rows set to On or Off decide for themselves.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.preset.toolt: Use the groups below: the switches decide. Immersion mode: a hand-picked set of lights that would really flicker (torches, lanterns, fire, campfires, candles, furnaces, froglights, glow lichen and glow berries, shroomlight, magma, lava and lava buckets, nether portal, crying obsidian, end portal and gateway, enchanting table, ender chest, brewing stand); glowstone, sea lanterns, redstone, amethyst and sculk stay steady. Flicker all lights: every light, even rows set to Off. In the last two modes the switches below are ignored (shown in grey).
headys_lumen.config.flicker.speed.toolti: Speed for every light that flickers because of this tab. 1 = a slow waver, 20 = a fast, nervous flame.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.strength.too: How much those lights dim at their darkest, as a share of their brightness.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.torche: Torches and soul torches, vanilla and modded (not redstone torches).
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.lanter: Lanterns and soul lanterns, vanilla and modded (not sea lanterns or jack o'lanterns).
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.fire.t: Campfires, candles and candle cakes, fire, soul fire, jack o'lanterns, lit furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.redsto: Redstone torches, redstone lamps and redstone ore (while it glows), and modded items with redstone in their name.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.sea.to: Sea lanterns, sea pickles and conduits.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.nether: Glowstone, shroomlight, magma blocks, crying obsidian, respawn anchors, lava (and lava buckets) and nether portals.
headys_lumen.config.flicker.group.cave.t: Glow lichen, glow berries, amethyst clusters and buds, sculk sensors and sculk catalysts.
